structure: Part 9, Decisions ledger. Read in full: src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/decisions.json (1433 lines, schema_version 1, one array of 84 decisions d-001 to d-084) and src/server/app/sets/high-risk-plants/spec/panel/README.md (32 lines). Each decision has id, subject {kind conflict|behaviour, id}, ruling (resolve|adopt|park), resolution, rationale, decidedBy (panel|sam), dissent, escalate, supersedes, supersededBy, decidedAt and status. Counts: 40 conflict rulings (37 panel, 3 sam), 21 behaviour adopts (20 panel, 1 sam), 23 behaviour parks (18 panel, 5 sam). Every decision is dated 2026-09-06, status current, escalate false, and none supersedes or is superseded by another. The README says the ledger is the only place a ruling lives, names the two evidence files (rulings.json, critic.json, out of scope here), lists the standing rulings for the first pass (users, sign-in models, agents, delegation of authority, plant-operator registration and who notifies out of phase; bulk upload out of phase; both parked not rejected) and gives the spec-add-decision.sh command for superseding a ruling. Claims run ledger-level first, then the README, then each decision in ledger order (one to three claims per decision, each naming the decision id, subject, ruling, who decided and when); rationales are claimed where they state a sourced rule or a verified fact about the code, and dissents where they record a losing option. The panel's evidence files are not read, as the scope says.
